chapter_title: Concerning the Four Things over which People kill each other.
chapter_note: This chapter reads as a homiletic/moral catalogue of “worldly” pursuits (food, sex, wealth, war/glory) followed by direct exhortation (“I say to you… accept faith…”) and a brief mortality conclusion. It lacks the substrate’s hallmark cosmos→cosmos correspondential mapping (degree-structures, realm↔metal/taste/form correspondences, systematic cosmography). The light/dark language appears only as soteriological application within a second-person address, consistent with later pastoral/application material; no extractable core block is present.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue-frame opener (“Once again he speaks to his disciples”) is a compiling-community hagiographic wrapper, not the older teaching substrate.

Ethical/social observation about bodily eating and “obsession,” with no internal cosmological correspondential mapping; reads as moral instruction/catalogue rather than impersonal cosmological exposition.
Continuation of the fourfold moral catalogue (sexual intercourse/fornication). No cosmic architecture or systematic correspondences; no frame/citation markers, but still application-level ethics.
Wealth/boasting is treated as worldly vanity; again, moralizing catalogue rather than substrate-style cosmology.

War, disputes, tyranny, and pursuit of a “name in the world” are presented as human social behaviors; this is application to the contemporary human sphere (cosmos→world pointing), not cosmos→cosmos mapping.

Generalizing application statement about “All people… who side with these four… on every tongue… in the world”; the rhetoric targets present human behavior, aligning with application/pastoral voice rather than substrate description.

Direct exhortation and audience address (“I say to you… whoever will accept faith…”). Although it uses Manichaean dualist language (“separates the light from the darkness”), it is embedded in a first-person, missionary/applied register (“physician whom I have brought”), not an impersonal systematic cosmological teaching block.
Concluding moral/eschatological truism about impermanence and death (“they will not remain… for eternity”); application-level conclusion with no cosmological mechanics.
